The clash of steel and hiss of fire filled the air as Phainon and Mydei fought their way through the dense fogs of Januspolis. The Followers of Strife were relentless in their pursuit, their chaotic energy cackling like thunder as madness overtook them.

Suppressing a wince, Phainon struck them down one by one, moving on instinct alone—his thoughts drowned out in the midst of the battle while dispatching any of the titankin who’d gotten a tad too close.

As if sensing his fatigue, Mydei abruptly changed his stance, mercilessly striking down an enemy who’d managed to sneak behind him before he had the time to react,“Getting tired, Deliverer?” Mydei taunted, his voice laced with a hint of challenge.

A breathless laugh left Phainon’s lips as he retorted, “Of course not. In fact, I’ve only just begun, Mydei. You’ll find out I don’t tire so easily.”

At that the prince scoffed, but with after a brief exchange of knowing glances, they’d both fell into a familiar rhythm, fighting side by side like a well rehearsed dance.

Phainon’s blade carved through the air with deadly accuracy, and as he made another precise cut, Mydei was already there, sweeping in to dispatch a foe who had tried to take advantage of Phainon’s opening. Without a word, they shifted positions—Phainon taking the front, Mydei darting to the side to cover him. Every move felt instinctive, their silent understanding of each other blossoming in moments like this.

When Mydei ducked under a brutal swing, Phainon was right there, parrying the blow before it could land. Mydei’s free hand shot forward, grabbing the enemy by the wrist and twisting it with practiced precision, sending the soldier crashing to the ground. Their movements were seamless, a perfect balance of offense and defense, as if they had become extensions of each other in the heat of battle.

Alas, even they couldn’t hold out forever. The onslaught was relentless, their enemies closing in from all sides like a tightening noose. “Keep moving!” Mydei barked, his voice sharp and commanding as he delivered a brutal strike to an opponent’s neck. The sickening snap that followed grated on Phainon’s ears, but there was no time to dwell on it.

They were being overwhelmed, even with their best effort they were still faltering under the sheer number of foes pressing in.

“Mydei we can’t hold on any longer!” Phainon all but yelled, to which Mydei didn’t respond to, busy cleaving through the titankin who just kept on coming.

“ They’re regrouping—don’t let them box us in!” Mydei’s voice was as sharp as his strikes, though Phainon caught the slight strain beneath his usual confidence.

Now it was Phainon’s turn not to respond. He was too focused on the path ahead, his gaze catching on a shadowed structure partially obscured by vines and rubble—a temple, ancient and untouched by time. It was their only chance.

“There!” He shouted over his shoulder, jerking his head toward the structure. Mydei glanced up, his expression hardening.

“A dead end? That’s your plan?”

“It’s shelter!” Phainon shot back, already making a run for the temple’s crumbling steps

With a frustrated growl, Mydei followed, hurling a final burst of fire toward their pursuers before ducking inside. The heavy stone doors groaned as they slammed shut behind them, muffling the chaotic sounds of the fight outside.

Inside, the silence was almost deafening. The faint glow of strange glyphs lit the massive chamber, casting flickering light across the worn stone walls. Phainon leaned against the door, catching his breath as Mydei paced in tight, irritated circles.

“This is your idea of a strategy? Running into some cursed ruin with no way out?” Mydei snapped, his tone biting.

“You’re welcome to go back out there and face them alone,” Phainon retorted, his calm tone doing little to mask his own exhaustion.

Sighing, Phainon continued, “Tribbie should eventually realize something went wrong and send someone out for us. Now all we have to do is wait.”

Mydei scoffed, running his hand through his sweat-dampened hair as he surveyed the ancient chamber. “Wait? That’s your brilliant solution? Wait while those titankin claw their way in hoping for a rescue?” Mydei snorted, crossing his arms as he leaned against a nearby pillar. “You’d think the great Deliverer would have more than that up his sleeve.”
